item.title: Israeli forces push 8 km into south Lebanon toward Litani River
item.description: Israeli ground forces have advanced roughly eight kilometers into southern Lebanon along the coast toward the town of Bayada, according to a United Nations official and Lebanon's defense minister, as Israel's military leadership signals its intent to seize and hold territory stretching to the Litani River — an area amounting to nearly a tenth of the country.

item.title: Zelenskyy signs 10-year defense pact with Qatar, capping Gulf tour
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy wrapped up a whirlwind three-day tour of the Gulf this week, signing defense cooperation agreements with Saudi Arabia and Qatar and reaching a security pact with the United Arab Emirates — all while pressing oil-rich partners to help avert a looming diesel crisis back home.

item.title: Iranian strike damages major UAE aluminum plant, workers injured
item.description: Emirates Global Aluminium's Al Taweelah site in Abu Dhabi, the largest aluminum-producing complex in the United Arab Emirates, sustained significant damage on Saturday during Iranian missile and drone attacks, according to a Reuters report. A number of workers at the facility were injured in the strike, Aluminium Today reported.

item.title: IDF needs 'a few more weeks' to degrade Iran's military, Israeli official says
item.description: A senior Israeli security official told ABC News that the Israel Defense Forces need "a few more weeks" to fully degrade Iranian military capabilities, casting doubt on the prospect of a swift diplomatic resolution to the month-old war even as President Donald Trump extended a deadline threatening Iran's energy infrastructure.

item.title: Explosion hits near Erbil airport as Kurdistan attacks persist
item.description: An explosion was heard Saturday morning near the international airport of Erbil, the capital of Iraq's autonomous Kurdistan Region, according to an AFP journalist on the ground. A witness reported seeing smoke rising from the area near the airport perimeter. No details on casualties or the cause of the blast were immediately available.

item.title: Trump weighs stripping NATO voting rights over Iran war dispute
item.description: President Donald Trump escalated his confrontation with NATO on Friday, telling a major investment conference in Miami that the United States may no longer come to the defense of alliance members who refused to support American military operations against Iran. Speaking at the Future Investment Initiative Priority Summit on March 27, Trump called NATO allies' absence from the now month-old conflict a "tremendous mistake" and questioned the fundamental bargain underpinning the 77-year-old alliance.

item.title: Houthis fire missiles at Israel, warn of Red Sea blockade
item.description:
Yemen's Houthi rebels launched their first missile attack on Israel early Saturday, firing a barrage of ballistic missiles at what they described as "sensitive Israeli military installations" in the country's south, and warned that closing the Bab el-Mandeb Strait remains on the table — a move that could compound what is already a severe global energy crisis.

The Israeli military said it intercepted a missile launched from Yemen, reporting no casualties. Brigadier General Yahya Saree, the Houthi military spokesperson, claimed responsibility in a broadcast on the group's Al-Masirah channel, declaring the attacks would continue "until the aggression on all resistance fronts comes to a halt". The strikes mark the Houthis' formal entry into the month-old war between the United States, Israel, and Iran.

item.title: Israeli airstrike kills three journalists in southern Lebanon
item.description:
An Israeli airstrike on a media vehicle near the town of Jezzine in southern Lebanon killed at least three journalists on Saturday, according to Lebanese media reports, in one of the deadliest single attacks on press workers since the current round of fighting began in early March.

Ali Shoeib, a prominent correspondent for the Hezbollah-affiliated Al-Manar TV, and Fatima Ftouni, a reporter for Al-Mayadeen, were among those killed when the strike hit the car they were traveling in. A third victim, reported to be Ftouni's brother and cameraman, also died in the attack, according to the Lebanese newspaper L'Orient-Le Jour, as cited by Spain's El País. A fourth occupant, identified as Shoeib's son, was also in the vehicle.

item.title: Iran says it targeted US vessel near Oman as war widens
item.description:
Iran's military said Saturday that it had targeted a U.S. logistics vessel near the Omani port of Salalah, marking another escalation in a monthlong conflict that has now drawn in Yemen's Houthi rebels and rattled Gulf states from Saudi Arabia to the UAE.

"A logistics vessel supporting the aggressive US army was targeted by the armed forces of the Islamic Republic of Iran at a considerable distance from the port of Salalah in Oman," Ebrahim Zolfaghari, a spokesman for Iran's central military command, said in a statement carried by Iranian state television, according to AFP.

item.title: 'No Kings' protests sweep Europe as London draws half a million
item.description: Protesters poured into the streets of cities across Europe, Australia, and beyond on Saturday, extending the American "No Kings" movement into a global day of action against what demonstrators described as authoritarian governance and the ongoing U.S. military conflict in Iran.

item.title: Debris from intercepted Iranian missile injures 5 in Abu Dhabi
item.description:
The United Arab Emirates intercepted six ballistic missiles and nine unmanned aerial vehicles launched from Iran on March 27, the UAE Ministry of Defence announced, as the Gulf nation endures near-daily attacks that have now stretched into a second month.

The interception brought the UAE's cumulative defense tally since the start of the conflict to 378 ballistic missiles, 15 cruise missiles, and 1,835 drones destroyed, according to the ministry. On Saturday morning, falling debris from another intercepted missile sparked two fires in the Khalifa Economic Zones Abu Dhabi, injuring five Indian nationals, according to CNN-News18.

item.title: Russian and Iranian foreign ministers weigh conflict settlement options
item.description: Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov spoke by phone on Friday with Iranian counterpart Abbas Araqchi to discuss the possibility of a diplomatic resolution to the month-long war between the United States, Israel, and Iran, as multiple diplomatic tracks gained momentum heading into the conflict's fifth week.

item.title: Bahrain says it intercepted 559 Iranian missiles and drones
item.description: Bahrain's Defense Force announced Saturday that its air defense systems have intercepted and destroyed a cumulative total of 174 missiles and 385 drones since Iranian attacks on the Gulf kingdom began on February 28. The latest figures mark a sharp increase from earlier this week, when Bahrain reported intercepting 154 missiles and 362 drones, underscoring the relentless pace of strikes nearly a month into the conflict.

item.title: IRGC claims US Marines killed in strike on Kuwait
item.description: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed Saturday that its naval forces struck US Marine positions on Kuwait's Bubiyan Island with a combined barrage of drones and ballistic missiles, alleging that "a large number" of American troops were killed. The Pentagon had not confirmed casualties at the time of reporting.

item.title: Israel strikes kill paramedics, journalists as Lebanon crisis deepens
item.description: The United Nations sounded urgent alarms on Friday over Lebanon's rapidly deteriorating humanitarian situation, with UNHCR warning the country is on the brink of a "humanitarian catastrophe" as Israeli strikes and ground operations enter their fourth week. More than 1.2 million people have been displaced since fighting escalated on March 2, including over 370,000 children uprooted at a rate of 19,000 per day, according to UN officials briefing reporters in Geneva.

item.title: Rosatom says Bushehr nuclear plant situation worsening after third strike
item.description: A series of strikes on Iranian nuclear facilities in recent days, including the country's only operational nuclear power plant, have intensified international alarm over the risk of a radiological incident, even as authorities report no radiation leaks so far.

item.title: China launches world's first floating deep-sea research island in Shanghai
item.description: China officially launched the world's first ultra-large floating deep-sea research facility in Shanghai on Saturday, the same week a Reuters investigation revealed that dozens of Chinese research vessels have been systematically mapping the ocean floor across the Pacific, Indian, and Arctic oceans in what naval experts say is preparation for potential submarine warfare against the United States and its allies.

item.title: Drone strike hits Kurdistan president's home in Duhok
item.description: A drone strike targeted the residence of Kurdistan Region President Nechirvan Barzani in the northern Iraqi city of Duhok on Saturday, prompting Iraqi Prime Minister Mohammed Shia al-Sudani to condemn what he called a "brutal attack" and order an immediate investigation, according to Reuters. No casualties were reported.

item.title: WHO says nine paramedics killed in southern Lebanon
item.description:
The World Health Organization said Saturday that nine paramedics were killed and seven others wounded in five separate attacks on healthcare teams in southern Lebanon, bringing the total number of health workers killed since the Israeli military escalation began on March 2 to 51.

WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus detailed the strikes in a post on X, saying medics were hit while on duty in five villages. In Zoutar al-Sharqiya, five health workers were killed and two injured, one critically. Two more were killed and three wounded in Kfar Tibnit. One paramedic died in each of Ghandouriyeh and Jezzine, while two were wounded in Kfar Dajjal.

"The repeated attacks on health care are severely disrupting the delivery of services in southern Lebanon," Tedros wrote, adding that "the only way to end these tragedies is to end attacks on health care, NOW".

item.title: Houthis launch first missile attack on Israel as U.S. Marines reach Middle East
item.description:
The USS Tripoli and roughly 2,500 Marines arrived in the Middle East on Friday as Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen launched their first missile attack on Israel since the war began, opening a new front in a rapidly expanding regional conflict now one month old.

U.S. Central Command announced Saturday that the Tripoli Amphibious Ready Group and the embarked 31st Marine Expeditionary Unit reached its area of responsibility on March 27, carrying approximately 3,500 sailors and Marines along with strike fighter aircraft and amphibious assault assets. The America-class amphibious assault ship had departed its homeport of Sasebo, Japan, earlier this month after Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth approved a CENTCOM request for reinforcements.
